t: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “C.B. King United States Courthouse”.

fable.w: This section only directs that references in federal records to a courthouse be deemed references to its new name. The word "regulation" might tempt a Yes, but it appears only in a boilerplate list of record types, not as a grant of rulemaking authority, and no party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any decision.

opus.w: This section only names a federal courthouse the "C.B. King United States Courthouse" in references to it in federal laws, maps, regulations and records. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision. Mentioning the word "regulation" in a list of documents does not authorize or require rulemaking, so it is not participation.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** The only possible pull toward "Yes" is that the section mentions a "regulation" and an official "record of the United States." That fails the definition. The section just says what a federal courthouse is to be called in references to it. No outside party is consulted, no rulemaking is required or authorized, and no hearing, comment period or right to sue is created.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a purely administrative renaming provision. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. It simply dictates how a specific building should be referred to in official records.
qwen_chat.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “C.B. King United States Courthouse”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that renaming a building involves public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a definitional amendment.
